title: Why Time Speeds Up As You Get Older

scenes.say: Remember when summer break felt endless? Now a whole year flies by. There's a reason.
Theory one is simple math. When you're five, one year is a fifth of your whole life.
scenes.heading: THEORY 1: MATH

scenes.say: At fifty, it's just two percent. Each year feels smaller.
Theory two is about memory. Your brain records new experiences in detail, but skips the routine ones.
scenes.heading: THEORY 2: MEMORY

scenes.say: Kids have tons of firsts. Adults repeat the same week. So when you look back, there's less to remember, and the time feels shorter.
It's called the holiday paradox. A new trip flies by while you're on it, but feels long when you look back.
scenes.heading: THE HOLIDAY PARADOX

scenes.say: So the trick to slowing time down? Do new things. A new route, a new hobby, a new place.
scenes.heading: THE TRICK

scenes.say: Does this year feel like it flew by?
